Advanced Features in cnma

Mahmood Developer

2025-11-06

Source: vignettes/advanced-features.Rmd
advanced-features.Rmd

Introduction

This vignette demonstrates advanced features of the cnma package, including:

  • Transportability analysis
  • GRADE quality weighting
  • Meta-regression
  • Publication bias assessment
  • Leave-one-out analysis

Setup 

library(cnma)

# Generate rich example data
data <- simulate_cnma_data(n_studies = 40, seed = 123)

Transportability Analysis

Transportability analysis weights studies by their similarity to a target population.

Define Target Population 

# Define characteristics of your target population
target_population <- data.frame(
  age_mean = 68,
  female_pct = 0.52,
  bmi_mean = 27.5,
  charlson = 1.8
)

Configure Transportability 

config <- setup_cnma(
  use_transport = TRUE,
  transport_metric = "mahalanobis",  # Distance metric
  transport_kernel = "gaussian",      # Weighting kernel
  transport_truncation = 0.02,        # Truncate extreme weights
  use_bayesian = FALSE,
  export_plots = FALSE
)

Run Analysis 

results <- run_cnma_analysis(
  data = data,
  target_population = target_population,
  config = config
)

Distance Metrics

Available metrics: - "mahalanobis": Accounts for correlations between covariates (recommended) - "euclidean": Simple Euclidean distance

Kernel Functions

Available kernels: - "gaussian": Smooth decay of weights - "tricube": Sharper cutoff for distant studies

GRADE Quality Weighting

Weight studies by evidence quality using GRADE assessments.

# Ensure your data has a 'grade' column
table(data$grade)

config <- setup_cnma(
  use_grade_weighting = TRUE,
  use_bayesian = FALSE,
  export_plots = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Quality weights (default): - High: 1.0 - Moderate: 0.75 - Low: 0.5 - Very low: 0.25

Risk of Bias (RoB2) Weighting 

# Ensure your data has a 'rob2' column
table(data$rob2)

config <- setup_cnma(
  use_rob2_weighting = TRUE,
  rob2_var = "rob2",
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Bias weights (default): - Low risk: 1.0 - Some concerns: 0.75 - High risk: 0.5

Study Design Weighting 

config <- setup_cnma(
  use_design_weighting = TRUE,
  design_var = "is_rct",
  design_weight_map = c(`1` = 1.0, `0` = 0.6),  # RCT vs observational
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Meta-Regression

Investigate effect modifiers with meta-regression.

Basic Meta-Regression 

config <- setup_cnma(
  run_metareg = TRUE,
  metareg_covariates = c("age_mean", "female_pct", "bmi_mean"),
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Spline Transformations

For non-linear relationships:

config <- setup_cnma(
  run_metareg = TRUE,
  metareg_covariates = c("age_mean", "female_pct", "bmi_mean"),
  metareg_spline_covars = c("age_mean", "bmi_mean"),
  metareg_spline_df = 3,
  metareg_spline_cv = TRUE,  # Cross-validation for df selection
  metareg_cv_folds = 5,
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Cluster-Robust Variance

For studies with shared characteristics:

config <- setup_cnma(
  run_metareg = TRUE,
  metareg_covariates = c("age_mean"),
  metareg_cr2 = TRUE,  # CR2 variance correction
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Publication Bias Assessment

Enable Publication Bias Tests 

config <- setup_cnma(
  enable_egger = TRUE,        # Network-level Egger test
  run_trimfill = TRUE,        # Trim-and-fill analysis
  run_selection_models = TRUE,
  run_copas = TRUE,
  pet_peese_min_k = 10,       # Minimum studies for PET-PEESE
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Leave-One-Out Analysis

Assess robustness by removing studies one at a time.

config <- setup_cnma(
  run_loo = TRUE,              # Leave-one-out
  run_loto = TRUE,             # Leave-one-treatment-out
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Inconsistency Assessment

Node-Splitting 

config <- setup_cnma(
  nodesplit_min_k = 10,
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

UME Inconsistency Model 

config <- setup_cnma(
  enable_ume = TRUE,
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Net Heat Plot 

config <- setup_cnma(
  run_netheat = TRUE,
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Bayesian Analysis

For more complex models and probabilistic inference:

config <- setup_cnma(
  use_bayesian = TRUE,
  bayes_link = "identity",
  bayes_likelihood = "normal",
  bayes_chains = 3,
  bayes_iter = 10000,
  bayes_warmup = 5000,
  bayes_nodesplit = TRUE
)

# Note: Requires JAGS installation
results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Bayesian Meta-Regression 

config <- setup_cnma(
  use_bayesian = TRUE,
  bayes_metareg_covariates = c("age_mean", "female_pct"),
  bayes_chains = 3,
  bayes_iter = 10000
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

SUCRA Analysis

Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking curve.

Basic SUCRA 

# SUCRA is calculated automatically with main analysis
# Access via results$results$main_nma

Bootstrap SUCRA

For uncertainty quantification:

config <- setup_cnma(
  sucra_boot = TRUE,
  sucra_boot_iter = 300,
  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

Combining Features

You can combine multiple advanced features:

# Comprehensive analysis
config <- setup_cnma(
  # Weighting
  use_transport = TRUE,
  use_grade_weighting = TRUE,
  use_rob2_weighting = TRUE,

  # Meta-regression
  run_metareg = TRUE,
  metareg_covariates = c("age_mean", "female_pct", "bmi_mean"),
  metareg_spline_covars = c("age_mean"),

  # Diagnostics
  run_loo = TRUE,
  run_loto = TRUE,
  enable_egger = TRUE,
  run_netheat = TRUE,

  # Output
  export_plots = TRUE,
  plot_dir = "comprehensive_plots",
  report_html = TRUE,

  # Performance
  parallel_strategy = "multicore",
  n_cores = 4,

  use_bayesian = FALSE
)

target <- data.frame(
  age_mean = 65,
  female_pct = 0.5,
  bmi_mean = 28,
  charlson = 1.5
)

results <- run_cnma_analysis(
  data = data,
  target_population = target,
  config = config
)

Exporting Results

Save Plots 

config <- setup_cnma(
  export_plots = TRUE,
  plot_dir = "my_nma_plots"
)

Generate HTML Report 

config <- setup_cnma(
  report_html = TRUE,
  report_file = "nma_report.html"
)

Write Manifest 

config <- setup_cnma(
  write_manifest = TRUE
)

Performance Optimization

Parallel Processing 

config <- setup_cnma(
  parallel_strategy = "multicore",
  n_cores = 4
)

# Or enable manually
cnma_parallel_on("multicore", workers = 4)
results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)
cnma_parallel_off()

Caching 

config <- setup_cnma(
  enable_cache = TRUE
)

Logging 

config <- setup_cnma(
  log_to_file = TRUE,
  log_file = "cnma_analysis.log"
)

Tips and Best Practices

  1. Transportability: Use when applying results to a different population
  2. GRADE Weighting: Use when you have quality assessments for all studies
  3. Meta-regression: Pre-specify covariates; beware of overfitting
  4. Publication Bias: Only meaningful with sufficient studies (>10)
  5. Bayesian Analysis: Provides probabilistic statements; requires JAGS
  6. Parallel Processing: Benefits diminish with small networks (<20 studies)

References

  • Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 2011.
  • Sterne JAC et al. RoB 2: a revised tool for assessing risk of bias in randomised trials. BMJ 2019.
  • Dias S et al. Network meta-analysis for decision-making. Wiley, 2018.
